decision.summary: The Federal Reserve voted to hold interest rates steady at 0 to 1/4 percent while continuing to taper its bond purchases.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January indicates that growth in economic activity slowed during the winter months, in part reflecting adverse weather conditions.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that winter weather temporarily slowed down economic growth at the start of the year.

changes.quote: Beginning in April, the Committee will add to its holdings of agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $25 billion per month rather than $30 billion per month, and will add to its holdings of longer-term Treasury securities at a pace of $30 billion per month rather than $35 billion per month.
changes.explanation: The Fed reduced its monthly asset purchases by another $10 billion total, continuing its gradual exit from quantitative easing.

changes.quote: To support continued progress toward maximum employment and price stability, the Committee today reaffirmed its view that a highly accommodative stance of monetary policy remains appropriate.
changes.explanation: The Committee signaled that low interest rates are still needed to help the economy recover.

changes.quote: With the unemployment rate nearing 6-1/2 percent, the Committee has updated its forward guidance.
changes.explanation: Because unemployment has gotten close to 6.5 percent, the Fed dropped that specific numerical threshold from its guidance in favor of a broader assessment.

tone_quotes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January indicates that growth in economic activity slowed during the winter months, in part reflecting adverse weather conditions.
Inflation has been running below the Committee's longer-run objective, but longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.

In light of the cumulative progress toward maximum employment and the improvement in the outlook for labor market conditions since the inception of the current asset purchase program, the Committee decided to make a further measured reduction in the pace of its asset purchases.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 11.85% APR costs about $49.38 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.78% and moved +10 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.28% would rise by about $17.65 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 6.7%, and employers added an average of 132k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.1% over the past year (February 2014); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +11 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.12% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed will likely continue reducing its monthly bond purchases in measured steps if economic data stays on track.
